column1: #! Every row needs a reason, and only two kinds may appear:
#! `zeo-only` (zeo defines a method CRuby has nowhere in the chain) and
#! `oracle-missing` (the dump could not reach the class at all). An arity
#! that simply disagrees with the oracle is a BUG in the parameter list --
#! it fails the test and cannot be recorded here. Regenerate with
#! Every PUBLIC method zeo declares on a class ruby also has now resolves,
#! so a public `zeo-only` row means one landed on the wrong class or was
#! invented -- check before accepting it. A PRIVATE one is a seam nothing
#! can reach, and cannot make the observable surface differ.
